title: Testing and validation in iterative development

slides.title: Recap: Software factories & trace analysis
slides.notes: Remind students that software factories orchestrate coding agents and produce structured execution traces. These traces are the primary artifact for diagnosing failures in iterative development.

slides.title: Iterative development loop overview
bullets: Agents repeat loop until criteria met
Each iteration produces a new trace
slides.notes: Explain that the loop is driven by autonomous agents; each pass generates a trace that can be analyzed for regressions or new failures.

slides.title: Testing role in each iteration
slides.notes: Testing is not a one‑off phase; it runs every iteration. Agents may generate tests from specifications or from observed behavior.

slides.title: Test types generated by agents
bullets: Mutation tests to assess suite quality
slides.notes: Agents can produce diverse test families. Property‑based and contract tests enjoy strong tooling support; mutation and stress tests are harder to automate fully.

slides.title: Validation strategies
slides.notes: Validation layers complement tests: static analysis catches syntax/type errors, dynamic checks assert contracts, runtime monitors flag unexpected states, and cross‑iteration comparison reveals regressions.

slides.title: Trace analysis workflow
slides.notes: Walk through each step: collection from the factory, parsing with a schema, filtering for error codes, clustering using similarity metrics, and finally producing a concise failure report.

slides.title: Common failure categories in agent logs
slides.notes: These five categories cover most observed failures. Emphasize that a single log may contain multiple categories; the analysis goal is to separate them with evidence.

slides.title: Worked example: Identify three failure causes

figure.code:
[2026-01-15 10:02:11] INFO  Agent started iteration 3
[2026-01-15 10:02:12] ERROR SpecParser: missing required field 'timeout'
[2026-01-15 10:02:13] WARN  ConfigLoader: env VAR_API_KEY not set
[2026-01-15 10:02:14] ERROR DependencyResolver: version conflict libfoo 1.2 vs 2.0
[2026-01-15 10:02:15] INFO  TestRunner: executing unit suite
[2026-01-15 10:02:16] FAIL  TestCase.test_auth: AssertionError: expected 200 got 401
[2026-01-15 10:02:17] ERROR MemoryMonitor: process exceeded 2GB limit
[2026-01-15 10:02:18] INFO  Agent aborted iteration 3

slides.notes: Demonstrate step‑by‑step: parse timestamps, filter ERROR/WARN/FAIL lines, map each to a failure category (spec mismatch, config drift, dependency conflict, resource exhaustion). Show how to cite line numbers as evidence.

slides.title: Hands‑on: Analyze a 2000‑line agent log
bullets: Run parser script to extract events
Write a short report with three causes
slides.notes: Students work in pairs. Provide a script that implements the five‑step workflow. TAs circulate to help with parsing regex and clustering parameters. Each pair submits a one‑page findings document.

slides.title: Check: Failure category matching

quiz.question: Which log line most clearly indicates a specification mismatch?
options: WARN ConfigLoader: env VAR_API_KEY not set
ERROR DependencyResolver: version conflict libfoo 1.2 vs 2.0
quiz.explanation: The SpecParser error shows the agent cannot understand the specification, a classic specification mismatch. The config warning is environment drift, the dependency error is a version conflict, and the memory error is resource exhaustion.

slides.notes: Quick poll to verify students can map log patterns to failure categories.

slides.title: Check: Trace analysis step order

quiz.question: What is the correct order of the trace analysis workflow steps?
options: Collect logs → Parse events → Filter errors → Cluster patterns → Summarize causes
Parse events → Collect logs → Filter errors → Summarize causes → Cluster patterns
Filter errors → Collect logs → Parse events → Cluster patterns → Summarize causes
Collect logs → Filter errors → Parse events → Summarize causes → Cluster patterns
quiz.explanation: The workflow starts with collection, then parsing, filtering, clustering, and finally summarizing. Other orders break dependencies between steps.

slides.notes: Reinforces the sequential nature of the analysis pipeline.

slides.title: Best practices for iterative testing & validation
bullets: Review failure reports before next iteration
slides.notes: Stress that automation reduces human latency, versioned traces enable regression comparison, thresholds prevent flaky decisions, and regular review closes the feedback loop.

slides.title: Tooling: log parsers & visualization
slides.notes: Introduce common tooling stack. Emphasize that structured logs make parsing reliable; visualization helps spot patterns across thousands of lines.

slides.title: Integrating analysis into CI/CD pipelines
bullets: Add trace analysis as a pipeline stage
Fail build on new failure categories
Trigger automated rollback on critical regressions
slides.notes: Show how the five‑step workflow can be a CI job. New failure categories can gate promotions; reports become traceable artifacts for audits.

slides.title: Key takeaways
bullets: Iterative loops produce rich traces for diagnosis
Three common categories: spec, config, dependencies, resources, logic
Hands‑on log analysis builds practical skill
Automation and CI integration close the loop
slides.notes: Recap the lecture flow: recap, loop, testing, validation, workflow, failure taxonomy, worked example, hands‑on activity, checks, best practices, tooling, CI integration. Remind students of upcoming lab evaluation.
